entries.bestFor: Yes/no questions, quick checks, spiritual dowsing
entries.notes: The most common method. Requires a weighted object on a chain. The direction of swing indicates yes/no.
Simplest method. Toss and interpret based on the spiritual feeling accompanying the result.

entries.bestFor: Finding objects, locations, water, hidden passages
entries.notes: Uses L-shaped rods or a Y-branch. The rods cross or dip when over the target.

entries.bestFor: Complex questions, symbolic answers, prophetic glimpses
entries.notes: The caster sets an intent before sleep. The dream contains a symbolic answer requiring interpretation. +2 if the caster keeps a dream journal.

entries.bestFor: Viewing distant places or people, surveillance
entries.notes: A darkened mirror or bowl of still water. The caster gazes until an image forms. Sensitive to light and noise.
Requires a clear quartz or glass sphere. Provides clear imagery. +1 if the ball has been consecrated.
A spread of cards reveals relationships between factors. Requires a deck with spiritual resonance.

Toss inscribed bones or lots and read the pattern. Effective for questions about the dead or spirits. A Beyonder may specialise in one method, gaining +1 when using it. This counts as a technique (see GURPS Techniques, p. B229). Specialisation does not penalise other methods — it simply reflects focused practice.
